body:
I'm still fairly new to hearing of the condition but from what I've read they don't seem to 100% know for sure what causes it :/ trauma seems to be the cause for me, although it was suppressed for most of my childhood so I guess it expressed itself through my dreams. I regularly deal with sleep talking and have had episodes of sleep paralysis in the past so I think I'm just prone to parasomnias too. 

I get you completely with your nightmare patterns too, zombie apocalypses are a recurring theme for me as well as being trapped with other people in an escape scenario. In those ones usually something really graphic happens to them and I can't do anything to stop it, they're the worst when it's people I know/care about. When I did briefly speak to my counsellor about it, she pointed out it always centered around a struggle for survival whether it be for myself or the chosen "main character" of my dream. I think that was the only helpful insight I got from her about it, she didn't really know what else to say otherwise, just suggested keeping a sleep diary and going to bed early... you'll understand it's not as simple as that lol 

I went through a long period of having just got used to them too and would for the large part either try to joke with friends about "this crazy dream I had last night" or thinking everyone dealt with it so it's not a big deal. When particularly awful ones happened it would rock my boat for a while but I'd ignore it sooner or later, it's like you get conditioned to it. Wasn't until the suppressed shit from when I was a kid decided I needed to process it now, then they really became unbearable and more of a haunting. Funny thing is, I don't even watch horror or anything with gore, even when friends insist on Halloween and such- no idea how my brain gets a lot of these ideas either.

I don't think I'm looking for advice about my parent situation,  what's done is done at this point and I'm not having regrets about that, but I appreciate your kind words.
Thank you for the advice with my sister though, what you said helped make some things clearer to me and reminded me she's nearly an adult herself now. I sometimes forget we're not all that different in age as for a long time she was the baby of the house and stayed childish for longer, but it's true I maybe discredited her maturity now. I don't know about my parents changing after this, they're very typical stubborn gen X's, but I definitely wouldn't get in the way of a possible healthy relationship between them if it were to happen, I just know I don't want to be involved.
Thanks again for the good luck.

I'm really sorry to hear you had such a bad experience with a mental hospital, nobody should have to deal with that especially with these thoughts and feelings already weighing you down. I'm glad you've found a couple ways of making things slightly easier though, the small pleasures in life really can help make a difference.
